LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 13.1.1 LISTENING COMPREHENSION: EXTENSIVE LISTENING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.1: Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Extensive Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Extensive Listening, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can we tell the main message in a song?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the key issues raised in songs, addressing land travel,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Extensive Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. listen attentively to songs on land travel,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Extensive Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use vocabulary identified from songs on land travel correctly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Extensive Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. Acknowledge the importance of extensive listening in communication.  Listen to songs on local and international land travel from audio recordings. Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned to enhanc the listening to the songs.  Respond to comprehension questions on key issues raised in the song, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views.  Pick out key issues raised from a song sung by the teacher or resource person on land travel,  Share ideas on the key issues addressed in the songs they have listened to using wall charts, How can we tell the main message in a song? 125  Identify vocabulary used in songs on land travel and infer their meaning from context,  Construct sentences orally using the vocabulary learnt. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to construct th sentences.  Sing choral songs on land travel.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Extensive Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Digital Literacy is enhanced when learner manipulates digital tools as they listen to songs based on local and international

land travel from audio recordings and respond to them.

Values:
Patriotism as the learner becomes conscious of their social and moral duties while picking out key issues raised from a song on

land travel

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Effective communication is strengthened as the learner listens to songs on local and international land travel from audio and

video sources.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify the key issues raised in songs, addressing land travel,
2. listen attentively to songs on land travel,
3. use vocabulary identified from songs on land travel correctly,
4. Acknowledge the importance of extensive listening in communication.  Listen to songs on local and international land travel from audio recordings. Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned to enhanc the listening to the songs.  Respond to comprehension questions on key issues raised in the song, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to construct th sentences.  Sing choral songs on land travel.

Remember the key question: How can we tell the main message in a song?
